title: The glory departed (1 Samuel 4)
hook: the ark is captured, Eli dies, and a baby is named "the glory is departed"

segments.voice: Yesterday, a boy in the dark at Shiloh, learning to answer. Your line was here am I. Did you let someone tell you something hard, all the way through? Today, the hard message comes true. Day seven hundred thirty.

A runner comes from the battlefield with his clothes torn and earth on his head. He runs straight into the city, and the whole city cries out. Eli, very old now, his eyes set so that he cannot see, is sitting on his seat by the road, waiting. His heart, the text says, trembled for the ark of God. Israel had lost a battle against the Philistines, and the elders had a plan: bring the ark of the covenant from Shiloh into the camp, so that it may come among us and save us. When it arrived, the soldiers shouted so loud the earth rang. Now the runner reaches the old man. Israel has fled. Your two sons are dead. And the ark of God is taken.
screen: `A RUNNER WITH EARTH ON HIS HEAD.` → `BRING THE ARK, IT WILL SAVE US.` → `THE ARK OF GOD IS TAKEN.`

segments.voice: It's the ark that breaks him. When the runner names the ark, Eli falls backward from his seat by the gate, his neck breaks, and he dies. And then the chapter does something unexpected. It doesn't stay with the generals or the priests. It goes to a woman in labor. Eli's daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Phinehas, is about to give birth. She hears all of it at once: the ark taken, her father-in-law dead, her husband dead. And the labor comes on her suddenly. The women attending her try to comfort her: fear not, you've borne a son. The text says she didn't answer, and didn't take it to heart. She has one thing left to do. She names the child Ichabod, saying, "The glory is departed from Israel." And the text says why: because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband. Then she says it again, as if once weren't enough: the glory is departed from Israel; for the ark of God is taken. Sit with what happened here. The elders carried the ark into battle so that it would save them. It didn't. The chapter doesn't soften it. In one day the ark is gone, the old priest at the gate is dead, and his two sons with him, and the one who names it plainly is a dying mother giving her son a name nobody would want. And yet the book doesn't end here. In the chapters that follow, the ark's story goes on, and it doesn't go the way the Philistines expected.
screen: `THE ARK CARRIED INTO BATTLE.` · `ELI FALLS AT THE GATE.` · `A MOTHER NAMES WHAT WAS LOST.` · `THE STORY DOESN'T END HERE.` · then, large: `THE GLORY IS DEPARTED FROM ISRAEL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with a loss of something grand. Not a small disappointment. Something bigger than you that you counted on. A place that closed. A community that broke apart. A hope you carried for years. A version of a family, or a country, or yourself. Settle, and let it come to mind. Don't rush to the bright side. Do what Phinehas's wife did, and give it a true name, even just in your head. Say what's gone. Then breathe, and let the naming be enough for now. If you pray, you can bring that loss to God exactly as it is. The bell holds the time.
Ichabod. The name a dying mother gives her son on the day the ark is taken and Eli dies, explained by her own words: the glory is departed from Israel. Today's word.
Your line: name it plainly. Today, if someone tells you about something they've lost, don't hurry them toward the bright side. Let them name it. Day seven hundred thirty.

howItsDone: Jews read the loss of the ark at Aphek as part of the Former Prophets, and some readers take the elders' plan to carry the ark into battle as a warning against treating holy things as charms.

original.note: Hebrew: Ichabod, the name the text explains with 'the glory is departed from Israel'.

trapdoor: what you thought: an odd old name.
what it means: the name a dying mother gives her son on the day the ark is lost and Eli and his sons die.
what a scholar hears: the text explains the name twice, and the second time gives one reason only: for the ark of God is taken.
recall: son of Abinoam, called to lead

notes: Verify JPS 1917 wording of 4:21 'The glory is departed from Israel' (certain in the KJV).
'So that it may come among us and save us' (4:3) is paraphrased close to the text without quotation marks; the source is listed with quoted null.
Eli's age (4:15) is in the text but is left out; 'very old' stands in.
'The chapters that follow' (1 Samuel 5–6) are only gestured at; the ark's return is not taught.
howItsDone 'many readers take...' is an interpretive claim; a Keeper may soften to 'some readers'.

Original: אִי־כָבוֹד as in 4:21. The meaning of the prefix (often glossed 'where is' or 'no') is NOT taught, under the etymology rule; the note relies only on the text's own explanation. Confirm vocalization and stress.
The day avoids saying what the mother felt; it reports only that she did not answer or regard it (4:20).

Editor: cut the narrator's 'lucky charm' verdict (the text says only 'that it may save us') and the claim that the Shiloh sanctuary was gone in one day (1 Samuel 4 does not say so); 'the only one who names it truthfully' softened; howItsDone 'many readers' changed to 'some readers'; trapdoor and screen head adjusted to match.
